catalogRevisions.note: X5 and D19: each Rust catalog revision pinned with the Go revision it stands for (neutral-host-tool-names). platform and standalone are the served catalogs (crate test catalog::tests::revisions_match_manifest checks both sides: the Go value is the revision of the un-renamed catalog). providerFixtures are the catalogs the provider-lifecycle fixtures publish, each observed one-to-one in the listed scenarios. The D19 divergence maps only these pinned pairs; any other revision stays a diff.

D10.summary: With standalone mutations disabled, Rust runs only tools whose effect is read instead of Go's enumerated gate list

D11.summary: Rust rejects enumerated invalid MCP calls without invocation audit writes; Go remains unchanged

D12.summary: Rust refuses task-aware calls at binding or admission before any durable operation record; Go persists the operation first (server.go:1642-1652)

D13.summary: Rust's redact_for_storage fails closed on any unmarked/open-schema durable content, replacing it with a redaction marker; Go's pinned reference persists it verbatim. Delivery to a caller (tasks/get, live or restored) is unaffected by this divergence.

D14.summary: Every Rust capability, built-in or external, follows one architecture: a Service Definition, a Service Provider mounted in one service context, and a Consumer; they differ only in distribution, trust and declared Go-observable contracts; built-in identities are unreachable by provider families; no observable change; M1-M7 capabilities are revised onto the seam before M8 starts

D15.summary: The ollama provider is out of the Rust migration scope: excluded from the M7 exit gate and the inventory; Rust behaviour unchanged

D16.summary: Rust validates a provider candidate before displacing other providers' family operations; a failed candidate leaves registry, catalog, bindings and MCP tools intact

D17.summary: Rust refuses a null provider input-request entry with 'nil InputRequest entry' instead of Go's SDK panic

D18.summary: Extend D12: a delegated callback child that never starts leaves no durable row; after a restart its handle is unknown

D19.summary: Rust publishes provider-neutral names for eight host tools (and packageName for incusPackage); the Go names stay hidden, deprecated aliases until cutover

D20.summary: For a corrupt compressed zstd block, extract_host_archive keeps Go's failure, prefix and tree, but the text after 'extract host archive: ' is the Rust decoder's own

D21.summary: Extends D19's map for M8b: reset_incus_stack is published as reset_virtualization_stack and provision_container.wslGpuLibs as hostGpuLibs; Go names stay hidden, accepted aliases until cutover. Also confirms D19's use on durable rows (M5 shape) and the secret sweep's catalog

D22.summary: Extends D19's map for M8c: get/delete_k8s_resource, get_k8s_resource_status, list_k8s_events, put_k8s_secret, exec_kubernetes_command, list_kubernetes_clusters, install_helm_chart and render_helm_template are published as get/delete_cluster_resource, get_cluster_resource_status, list_cluster_events, put_cluster_secret, exec_cluster_command, list_compute_clusters, install_cluster_package and render_cluster_package; Go names stay hidden, accepted aliases until cutover

D8.summary: Rust implements the stricter oauth-issuance contract instead of Go's token issuance

go-vs-go.purpose: harness self-validation: the pinned Go binary compared with itself must be clean and deterministic

go-vs-rust.purpose: T1 differential parity of the Rust candidate; items outside a gate's surfaces may fail until their milestone

cutover.description: Whole-agent cutover (task 6.1). Fails until every surface has passing Rust evidence and the inventory has no gaps, owned or not; later milestones add T2/T3/T4 suites here. It also requires each reviewed cutoverEvidence file (package first success, isolated external effects, rollback rehearsal, owners' cutover review) the parity-gate invariant names

m0.description: M0 exit: harness proven (Go-vs-Go clean x20, every canary caught), inventory captured with zero unowned gaps, every Rust item present and unverified

m1.description: M1 exit: harness valid (Go-vs-Go x20, canaries, inventory) and the Rust candidate matches Go on every CLI, config and lifecycle item (x5), and passes the Go black-box startup tests; other surfaces may still differ (M2+)

m2.description: M2 exit: harness valid (Go-vs-Go x20, canaries, inventory); the Rust candidate matches Go on every CLI, config, lifecycle, HTTP, MCP wire and auth item (x5), including the generated wire corpus and the authz store cross-read; the Go black-box tests and the go-sdk real client pass against Rust; other surfaces may still differ (M3+); the declared divergence D8 (oauth-issuance) passes its Rust contract suite and every Rust canary is caught

m3.description: M3 exit: harness valid (Go-vs-Go x20, canaries, inventory); the Rust candidate publishes every catalog cell identically to Go (names, descriptors, schemas, edges, revision) and matches Go on every scenario of every surface (x5), including the read-only host tools, argument validation, the standalone mutation set and the X2 rejected-call invariant; the go-sdk real client reads the catalog and calls read-only tools; the D8 and D10 contract suites and Rust canaries pass; catalog revisions match the reviewed manifest (X5)

m4.description: M4 exit: everything M3 requires, plus admission and tasks matching Go on every scenario (x5): canonical URIs and kinds, tenant scope, the admission matrix over every non-read tool (gate closed, stale revision, binding, unknown target) with X2, coordinator saturation N+k, min-memory/min-disk headroom, normal-class host reads, the task registry, input_required, and cancellation before start, mid-shim and after completion with zero orphans; the D12 contract suite and its Rust canaries pass

m5.description: M5 exit: M1-M4 regression gates plus all six provenance-bound durable-state and redaction validations; missing evidence fails closed.

m6.description: M6 exit: M1-M5 regression gates plus the single plan executor -- recipe/plan validation (valid and invalid corpora), execution-trace fault scripts (retry-then-success, permanent-failure-with-compensation, readiness-never-true-timeout, cancel-mid-node) and restart-mid-plan reconcile -- all matching Go byte-for-byte except the declared, scoped-out probe_http_endpoint cancellation-framing note in evidence/m6/README.md (not a Rust/Go behavioral divergence requiring a decision: both sides now interrupt a cancelled in-flight dispatch promptly, masked only on the exact terminal literal).

m8a.description: M8a exit (host domain): M1-M7 regression gates (Go-vs-Go x20, canaries, inventory, oracles, contracts, M5) plus every host-domain item matching Go (x5) at T1 shim-trace parity, the M7 provider surfaces, and T2 twin-sandbox parity: every T2 host-domain scenario (effects, cleanup and residue, and the M4 admission-rejected calls leaving the host unchanged) passes Go-vs-Go x20 and Go-vs-Rust x5, re-derived from committed receipts. Remaining host T2 gaps (WSL2 runner, Incus instances) stay owned in baseline/inventory/t2.json.

m8b.description: M8b exit (incus domain): the M8a gate (M1-M7 regression gates, host domain at T1 and T2) plus every incus-domain item matching Go (x5) at T1 shim-trace parity, every T2 incus-domain scenario in nested-Incus twins (create, mutate, read and delete of real containers and VMs, the stack reset, cleanup and residue, and the M4 admission-rejected incus calls leaving Incus unchanged) passing Go-vs-Go x20 and Go-vs-Rust x5 re-derived from committed receipts, and the Go baseline's live Incus tests (test/live) passing against Go and Rust inside the twins with a failing negative control.

m8c.description: M8c exit (kubernetes and cluster domains): the M8b gate plus every cluster-domain item matching Go (x5) at T1 shim-trace parity against the pinned, unchanged Go k3s provider, and every T2 cluster-domain scenario in k3s twins (create, mutate, read and delete of real Kubernetes objects in a single-node k3s, HelmCharts, helm template, guest storage prune and registry garbage collection, the cluster agent's install through a harness platform stub and the agent's own bridge relay, cleanup and residue, and the M4 admission-rejected kubernetes and cluster calls leaving k1 unchanged) passing Go-vs-Go x20 and Go-vs-Rust x5 re-derived from committed receipts.

goReference.note: CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, -buildvcs=false, fixed ldflags; reproducible for a given Go toolchain

rustCandidate.note: Hash of the binary that produced evidence/current; rebuild and rerun make parity-m1 after any Rust change.

go-vs-go.purpose: T2 harness self-validation: Go twins from one golden must agree

go-vs-rust.purpose: T2 effect, cleanup and no-unauthorized-effect parity of the Rust candidate
